correctness.rationale: The lower bound is exact: every E14-CFF is a 14-block Sperner family, and Sperner's theorem gives t(1,14)=6 because C(5,2)=10<14<=C(6,3)=20. The displayed fourteen distinct triples on [6], grouped into seven matching edges, satisfy endpoint incomparability and, for each edge, every one of the twelve off-edge blocks has a point outside the endpoint union. Hence they form an E14-CFF on six points. Proposition 5.8 of the primary paper gives t_e(E14)=t(1,7)=5, so t(E14)=6=t_e(E14)+1. A fresh independent bounded replay checked all seven edges and all 84 off-edge containment conditions; the infinite lower bound is theorem-based, not inferred from the finite check.
